description: An orchestrator's fan-out as ONE card: a summary line (how much finished, what it cost, when it should be over) and a grid of tiles — one tile per unit of work, with its worker, its state, its attempt count and a live countdown to its estimate. The surface renders the task list it is given and never polls or mutates anything: the host owns the data and the transport, the component owns its view. The injected TimeProvider drives the countdown AND the ticker that repaints it, so a test with a fake clock closes a second without sleeping and a finished fan-out arms no timer at all. The grid is an APG grid: ONE tab stop (a roving tabindex), the arrow keys walk the tiles in reading order, Home/End stay inside the current row and Ctrl+Home/Ctrl+End jump across the whole grid, PageUp/PageDown jump a page of rows. A tile is a native <button>, so Enter and Space activate it exactly once with no emulation (docs/keyboard-activation-convention.md). A state is never carried by colour alone: the tile paints an icon, a localized WORD and a tone. The detail follows the tile the reader focused (or pointed at) and carries the Retry and Cancel actions — the same actions a host would put on a row menu, reachable without a pointer. Hundreds of tasks mount a bounded window of tiles while the grid still declares its full aria-rowcount and every mounted row keeps its real aria-rowindex, so what a screen reader counts is the grid, not the window.

parameters.name: Class
parameters.description: Additional CSS class(es) for the root element.

parameters.name: Columns
parameters.description: How many tiles sit on one grid row, clamped to 1–8. Default 4. The value is also written onto the root as --tm-fan-out-columns, so the stylesheet lays the rows out with the same number the C# window uses. In ColumnsMode Auto the value is the FALLBACK before the first measurement arrives.

parameters.name: ColumnsMode
parameters.description: Whether Columns decides the grid outright (Fixed, the default — pure CSS plus the inline knob, no measurement) or the component measures its own grid through TmLayoutObserver and fits as many tiles of MinTileWidth as the width allows (Auto). The measured number drives BOTH the inline knob and the C# window math, so the rendered rows can never diverge from what a screen reader counts.

parameters.name: Compact
parameters.description: Whether the compact presentation is used: a tile keeps its label, its state word and its attempt badge and drops the countdown and the worker line. Default false. The grid keys, the detail and the actions are unchanged — compact hides information, never a way to act.

parameters.name: CostFormatter
parameters.description: Formats a cost given in MICRO-UNITS (1,000,000 is 1.00 of the currency). Null uses AiCostFormatter with Culture — the culture's own currency, with micro-unit precision below one hundredth of a unit. A host with a credit price model overrides it.

parameters.name: Culture
parameters.description: The culture that formats the costs and the clock times. Null (the default) means the current culture at render time. The countdowns are clock-style (m:ss) on purpose and are not localized.

parameters.name: DetailPresentation
parameters.description: Where the detail of the focused (or hovered) tile renders: Inline (the default) keeps it as a region below the grid; Popover anchors the same content to the tile in an overlay panel that closes on Escape and hands the focus back — the better shape for a narrow, measured grid, where an in-flow detail would push the tiles out of sight.

parameters.name: Filter
parameters.description: The state filter, two-way bound with FilterChanged (@bind-Filter). Default All. A host that pins it keeps control: the reader's pick reports the change and the next render from the host decides.

parameters.name: FilterChanged
parameters.description: Fires with the new filter when the reader picks one in the filter bar.

parameters.name: HeadingLevel
parameters.description: The heading level of the rendered title, clamped to 2–6. Default 3.

parameters.name: MinTileWidth
parameters.description: The width one tile needs in ColumnsMode Auto, in CSS pixels; the measured grid fits as many tiles of this width (plus the gap) as it allows, clamped to 1–8. Default 144 — the px equivalent of the stylesheet's --tm-fan-out-tile-min-inline-size (9 rem at a 16 px root). Values below 96 px are read as 96 px. The value is also written onto the root as --tm-fan-out-tile-min-inline-size, so a host can restyle the tile without a CSS override.

parameters.name: OnCancel
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks to cancel a task — the action lives in the tile's detail and is offered only while CanCancel holds. The component does not change the task.

parameters.name: OnRetry
parameters.description: Raised when the reader asks for a retry of a failed task — the action lives in the tile's detail and is offered only while CanRetry holds. The component does not change the task: the host owns the data and re-renders with the retried value.

parameters.name: ShowFilter
parameters.description: Whether the state filter bar is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: ShowSummary
parameters.description: Whether the summary line is rendered. Default true. It carries the finished / running / failed counts, the total of the priced tasks and the estimate of the last active one.

parameters.name: ShowTitle
parameters.description: Whether the heading is rendered. Default true.

parameters.name: Tasks
parameters.description: The units of work the orchestrator split the job into. Each tile is one entry; the summary counts the same list. Null or empty renders the localized empty state. The component never mutates the list and never reorders it — the grid paints the host's order, because that order is the host's own progress.

parameters.name: TimeProvider
parameters.description: The clock the countdowns and the repaint ticker read. Null uses the container's TimeProvider and falls back to System — the host's clock always wins over the machine's.

parameters.name: Title
parameters.description: The heading above the surface. Null renders the localized default ("Fan-out"); the heading also names the card, so the name a reader hears is the one they see.

parameters.name: VisibleTaskLimit
parameters.description: How many tiles may be mounted at once. Default 60; 0 (or a negative value) mounts the whole filtered list. Above the limit the grid mounts a window of whole rows that follows the focused tile, while aria-rowcount keeps declaring the filtered total — hundreds of tasks stay scrollable and cheap.

examples.title: A fan-out a host feeds from its queue
The tasks a host builds

notes: The surface renders the snapshot it is given; it never polls, fetches or mutates a task.
The injected TimeProvider drives the countdown and the repaint ticker: a test with a fake clock closes a second without sleeping, and a finished fan-out arms no timer.

Columns is the layout authority in Fixed mode: the C# window and the stylesheet read the same number, so a host that needs fewer tiles on a phone binds Columns rather than relying on a container query.

ColumnsMode Auto measures the grid's own box through the shared TmLayoutObserver and fits as many tiles of MinTileWidth as the width allows: ONE measured number drives the inline knob, the aria-colcount and the window math, so a phone never scrolls the grid sideways. Before the first measurement the clamped Columns stands.

DetailPresentation Popover anchors the same detail content to the focused tile in an overlay panel: Escape closes it and hands the focus back to the tile; an outside pointer closes it without pulling focus.

An active task that started without an estimate paints the elapsed read-out ("running for 2 min") on the tile, in the aria-label and in the detail — the ticker arms for it, so the read-out repaints every second without a host round-trip.
One polite live region announces a filter change, a moved focus and a retry or cancel request; the tiles themselves are native buttons with one roving tab stop.
